s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pancreatic syndrome with recent onset of hyperglycemia and abdominal symptoms in a patient with a history of diabetes and cardiovascular disease
salient_findings: Swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on imaging
Recent increase in plasma glucose and hemoglobin A1c
key_facts: 67-year-old man with a 3-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus
Managed with metformin and glimepiride
Prior percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction 2 months earlier
40-year smoking history, quit after myocardial infarction
Four episodes of bloody diarrhea daily
No abdominal pain or fever
Normal white-cell count, bilirubin, and liver function tests
Plasma glucose rose from 258 mg/dL to 449 mg/dL
Hemoglobin A1c increased from 7.3% to 8.0%
Microalbuminuria of 50.7 mg/day
Anti–glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies were negative
Elevated serum amylase and lipase
Swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on imaging

shortlist.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on imaging

shortlist.label: Acute pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum amylase and lipase, and recent onset of abdominal symptoms

shortlist.label: IgG4-related pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum IgG4 and clinical presentation consistent with IgG4-related disease

shortlist.label: Chronic pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of smoking and prior episodes of abdominal symptoms

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Newly diagnosed extensive ulcerative colitis and recent onset of pancreatic symptoms

raw.rationale: Elevated serum amylase and lipase, swelling of the pancreas with a peripheral rim on imaging, and the patient's recent onset of extensive ulcerative colitis are consistent with IgG4-related pancreatitis, although the serum IgG4 level is within the reference range, the overall clinical presentation and imaging findings support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
rejected.why: While similar to IgG4-related pancreatitis, the lack of specific autoantibodies and the presence of ulcerative colitis suggest a more specific diagnosis of IgG4-related pancreatitis

rejected.label: Acute pancreatitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not indicate a typical acute pancreatitis presentation, such as severe abdominal pain and elevated white-cell count

rejected.label: Chronic pancreatitis
rejected.why: The patient's recent onset of symptoms and lack of long-standing pancreatic dysfunction suggest a more acute process

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis-associated pancreatitis
rejected.why: While the patient has ulcerative colitis, the pancreatic findings are more suggestive of a primary pancreatic process, such as IgG4-related pancreatitis, rather than a secondary process related to the ulcerative colitis
